credit: Written for the app from the Port Vesper city data, an original setting.

entries.title: Station night
entries.text: On station night the rings dim, the Low Ring's music bars and late kitchens are the only loud places aboard, and the Meridian slides past the Great Window like a lit city.

entries.title: Morning on the station
entries.text: In the morning the Ring Bakehouse sells out of cardamom buns, the first shuttle of the day leaves the Departures Hall on the hour, and everyone checks the departures board twice.

entries.title: No weather aboard
entries.text: Port Vesper has no weather: the rings are climate-controlled, and the nearest thing to rain is the misting in the Garden Ring's coffee plantation.

entries.title: Earth time
entries.text: The station still counts years by the Earth calendar, so every meeting with the Meridian's voyage years starts a small argument.

entries.title: Evenings on the Market Ring
entries.text: In the evening the Market Ring is all noise: coffee houses pouring the Gate Six blend, spice stalls, tailors haggling, and station red that is better than anyone on the Meridian admits.

entries.title: The Concourse
entries.text: On the Concourse the traders' hotels and customs desks never close, and "mind the gate" is how the station says goodbye to anyone heading for a shuttle.

entries.title: The Yards
entries.text: In the Yards every welder signs their first mask and hangs it from the ceiling of the Rivet, and the canteen's yard pie is the size of a welding mask.

entries.title: The Great Window
entries.text: At the Great Window the Meridian turns in the dark, and proposing there with the ship passing behind is the station's favourite romantic cliche.

entries.title: The Old Hull
entries.text: In the Old Hull, all scuffed panels and stencilled deck numbers, every photo of the founding crew of fourteen shows fifteen people, and nobody can say who the last one is.

entries.title: Arrival Day
entries.text: Arrival Day marks the day Port Vesper caught up with the Meridian after a fourteen-year chase: a toast at the Departures Hall, and station families visiting their Meridian cousins.

entries.title: Midwinter
entries.text: At Midwinter there are candles in every window, mulled wine from the Garden Ring, Sheep Deck lamb for those who can afford it, and presents swapped with Meridian friends.

entries.title: Yards Day
entries.text: On Yards Day the yard crews have the day off and a parade of drones flies down the Concourse.

entries.title: At work on the station
entries.text: Port Vesper trades for a living, and every shift ends with somebody saying "caught up" about a deal that finally came through.
